title: Denying Self
definition: Denying Self is the disciple's surrender of self-rule, selfish ambition, and sinful independence in order to follow Christ.
summary: Denying Self is the believer's renunciation of self-rule in order to follow Jesus as Lord.
christFocus: Jesus Christ calls His disciples to lose their lives for His sake and find true life in Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Denying self is the disciple's refusal to let self-rule, comfort, pride, or sinful desire govern life. Scripture connects following Jesus with saying no to the old self and yes to the Lord.

This is not self-hatred or denial of human dignity. It is surrender of false lordship so Christ can rule the whole person.

Jesus denied Himself in perfect obedience to the Father and gave His life for sinners. His disciples follow Him by laying down self-centered control.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This matters because modern life often treats self-expression as the highest good. Denying self corrects the lie that freedom is found in indulging every desire and shows that true life is found under Christ's lordship.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Identify one place where self-rule resists Christ. Surrender it through prayer and obedience, and remember that losing life for Jesus' sake is the path to true life.
